summary: Do not slice yet. Round-1 re-verification: F1 resolved—D4 defines the canonical registry, fields, participating scripts, orphan convention, and negative fixtures (lines 110-129, 278-281). F2 still open—the serial DAG does not isolate simultaneous runners sharing `.output/chrome-mv3` (lines 141-146, 285). F3 still open—the commands are split, but no rule defines their disjoint test-file sets (lines 223-226, 264-266). F4 resolved—the promise guarantee is restricted to type-aware `src/` linting with a failing fixture (lines 232-234, 295). F5 resolved as originally raised—stories, fingerprint replacement behavior, and scope are aligned (lines 48-49, 236-242, 297); however, the fix introduced a new high-risk interaction with the format migration. F6 resolved—Chrome 108 exact matching and boundary fixtures are required (lines 199-201, 287). F7 resolved—complete rendering, lazy content, fonts, timeout failure, and empty/partial-render fixtures are required (lines 188-192, 289). F8 still open—D8 and its fixture use tree equivalence, but line 309 still prescribes the rejected `git show --stat` proof. The fix scan found one additional high issue and no critical issue.
triage: review-gate SKILL.md § Triage governs: render EVERY finding as a full table row, never inside a dialog; then ask the ROUND before the rows — take every Proposed decision as it stands, or decide row by row — and `as proposed` ends the round in that ONE action; only if row-by-row was chosen, ask per finding with that row's Proposed decision as the first option, a reject or defer taking a free-text reason; echo back ONLY the rows that carried free text, and none if the round was decided by selection alone; max 2 rounds, append decisions.md and COMMIT it with this artifact.

findings.title: Open question: How are concurrent runner outputs isolated?
findings.body: The fix says the runner will “산출물 디렉터리를 지우고” and build once in the shared `.output/chrome-mv3`, then assumes consumers see “이 회차의 빌드가 만든 산출물.” That only orders one invocation. Two agents can overlap: runner A builds, runner B deletes or replaces the directory, and A's consumers then inspect partial output or B's artifact. The accepted F2 recommendation included concurrent attempts, but line 285's fixture ledger omits them.
findings.recommendation: Lock the entire clean-build-consume phase or build into a run-unique directory passed explicitly to every consumer. Add an overlapping-run fixture proving the second invocation is rejected or both runs remain isolated.

findings.title: Open question: What defines the browser-backed test set?
findings.body: D12 declares `bun run test` browserless and `bun run test:browser` browser-backed, but never defines a filename convention, registry, include/exclude globs, or metadata that selects those sets. The Testing Decisions then say the only Vitest configuration change is including all `scripts/**/*.test.mjs`. With the current `test: vitest run`, a literal implementation selects every script test; otherwise the implementer must invent the split. The proposed parity assertion is circular because “브라우저 없는 집합” itself has no defined source of truth.
findings.recommendation: Define one machine-readable classification, such as `.browser.test.mjs` plus explicit complementary Vitest globs. Make both commands and the parity check derive from it, and test that a browser fixture is excluded from `test` and required by `test:browser`.

findings.title: Open question: How do accessibility fingerprints survive formatting?
findings.body: The new baseline is “규칙 이름 + 파일 + 식별 가능한 위치,” with every new fingerprint failing. D8 separately requires the lint/gate setup before a repository-wide format commit. If an implementer uses Oxlint's natural line/column location, formatting—or merely inserting a line before a known violation—turns the unchanged violation into a removed fingerprint plus a new one. The hard gate then falsely blocks the format-only commit, or forces a baseline refresh that can bless a genuine replacement regression. The tests cover replacement diagnostics but not position-only movement.
findings.recommendation: Define a position-stable fingerprint, such as rule, file, and normalized diagnostic subject or explicit suppression ID; order baseline capture after the format migration; and add a fixture where only preceding layout/lines change while the same violation must remain recognized.

findings.title: The format-only proof still accepts evidence that does not inspect the change
findings.body: D8 and line 293 correctly require reproducing the pinned formatter and comparing trees, but the normative regression section still says “`git show --stat`으로 그 커밋이 포맷 외 아무것도 건드리지 않았음을 보인다.” A competent engineer can follow this later instruction and satisfy the plan with the exact proof F8 established as invalid. Tests passing cannot prove semantic equivalence outside their coverage.
findings.recommendation: Replace line 309 with the pinned-formatter tree-equivalence procedure and recorded tree hash. Keep `git show --stat` only as optional descriptive output, never as proof.

next_steps: Specify concurrency isolation for build artifacts and add the omitted overlapping-run fixture.
Define the authoritative browser-test classification used by both commands and parity checks.
Make accessibility fingerprints stable across the required format migration and test position-only movement.
Remove the stale `git show --stat` acceptance language from the regression section.
